facts.text: Brushy takes its name from the nearby Brushy Mountains, which are known for their dense vegetation and local topography.
The area around Brushy was originally part of the Cherokee Nation's lands in Indian Territory during the early nineteenth century.
The Kansas and Arkansas Valley railroad line arrived between 1888 and 1890, helping to spur early community formation in Brushy.
A Brushy post office opened on September 4, 1900, providing formal recognition and aiding local homestead operations for ten years.
Brushy is located in the foothills of the Brushy Mountains, which are part of the larger Ouachita mountain system.
The Rural Electrification Administration brought power lines to the Brushy area starting in 1935, improving farm productivity and daily life.
